_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Science (086), set 31/4/1, opener of series 31/4: nothing skipped (plan.txt lists no reference). 24 page images (cover announces 23 printed pages; idx 23, folio 24, is BLANK, confirmed at full size). idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 2 English instructions + Q1-2; English on EVERY EVEN index 2-22, Hindi on every odd index 1-21; odd-page tops checked, all Hindi, and every English page's last question continues on the next EVEN page (Q32 idx 14->16, Q35(A) idx 16->18, Q36(A) idx 18->20), so the parity holds throughout. This paper labels its internal choices (A)/(B) in upper case, and its case studies (i), (ii), (iii)(A) OR (iii)(B) - NOT the (a), (b), (c)(i)/(c)(ii) of 31/1/1 - so refs follow the printed labels (Q37i, Q37ii, Q37iiia, Q37iiib). Instruction (viii) prints NO count of internal choices, so the roster was built by walking the marking scheme (ms idx 2-12): OR after Q22, 25, 27, 34, 35, 36, 37(iii), 38(iii), 39(iii) = 9 alternatives, each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper. The scheme's two further ORs inside Q22(B) (sulphide ore OR carbonate ore) and Q25(B) (I bifocal OR II convex lens) are alternative ANSWERS to one question, not question alternatives, and the paper prints no OR there. All 20 Section-A answers are CBSE's own, read off the scheme page image (ms idx 2); each was also re-derived and agrees. No void note anywhere in the scheme. Decimal points on this paper are ORDINARY full stops (Q32 table: 1.62).

(iv) How can ‘A’ be obtained from ethanol ?

(v) Name the gas produced when compound ‘A’ reacts with washing soda.
